title: Neuroendocrine Pair-Bonding Causal Atlas
research_questions: Which receptor and mesolimbic circuit perturbations selectively alter partner preference during formation versus maintenance?
How do dopamine, oxytocin, vasopressin, sex-steroid, and stress-axis variables interact over the bond trajectory?
Can a prespecified partner-cue neural representation be compared across prairie voles and humans without equating their behaviors?

hypotheses.claim: OXTR/AVPR1A perturbation selectively reduces partner-cue preference after locomotion and general social approach controls.
NAc D1/D2 perturbations have phase-specific effects on partner preference and persistence.
VTA-NAc dopamine response is more partner-selective than matched stranger and nonsocial reward responses.
Endocrine and stress-axis state moderates but does not replace circuit-level prediction of partner selectivity.
Partner-cue neural representations replicate across sessions and remain distinct from familiar-person and nonsocial reward representations.
A low-dimensional feature geometry is directionally shared across vole neural readouts and human imaging, with species-specific deviations.

human.primary_endpoint: cross-session partner-versus-familiar neural decoding and region-level contrast

analysis.animal: mixed-effects phase-by-perturbation model with block random effects
analysis.human: cross-validated multivoxel decoding plus hierarchical ROI model
analysis.cross_species: feature-space representational similarity plus hierarchical Bayesian shared-effect model
analysis.power: pilot-variance-based a priori calculation; planning targets are not observed results

safety.animal: IACUC/3R review, minimized separation, humane endpoints
safety.human: IRB, informed consent, MRI safety, no hormone or circuit manipulation, privacy-preserving data governance

unknowns_to_inherit: temporal order of peptide and dopamine effects
human_review_requirements: genetic privacy if optional genotyping is used
no clinical or relationship prediction claims
